sessionTitle: So you want to become an MVP?

announcements.name: Three-step path to MVP
announcements.shortDescription: To pursue the award: be an expert, do what you love, and let the program know, since nomination must come from a Microsoft employee or an existing MVP.
announcements.longDescription: The session wraps up by summarizing three simple steps to become an MVP: be an expert, do what you love, and let the program know. To be awarded MVP status, you have to be nominated either by a Microsoft employee or by an existing MVP. The closing advice is to do what you love, share that, and contribute to the community.

announcements.name: Program scale
announcements.shortDescription: The MVP program has run for over 30 years and now spans more than 4,000 award recipients across 96 countries and nearly 50 languages.
announcements.longDescription: The Microsoft MVP (Most Valuable Professional) program has been around for over 30 years and spans the globe. Today it includes more than 4,000 influencers covering 96 countries and a little over 49, almost 50, languages. The program looks for growing communities in every part of the world and invites locals to potentially become the next recipient.

announcements.name: Build participation
announcements.shortDescription: Over 100 MVPs are contributing at this Build event as speakers and lab helpers.
announcements.longDescription: Becoming an MVP can open doors, and over 100 MVPs are participating at Build by speaking, helping with labs, and doing a variety of other activities. MVP benefits also include receiving NDA information before the public, connecting to product groups for roadmaps and insider information, and giving feedback to those product groups. MVPs also join a global community of 4,000-plus members and receive exclusive invites to events such as the annual MVP Summit in Redmond.

announcements.name: Learn more resource
announcements.shortDescription: Staff directed attendees to aka.ms/mvp/learn for details on the program and how to contribute.
announcements.longDescription: Attendees are directed to aka.ms/mvp/learn to learn more about the MVP program and how to contribute. The speaker emphasizes that you don't need to be a Microsoft person—you can be an expert in open source or content creation—and that there is always a way to contribute, whether through blogs, videos, or other community-engaging activities.
